title: love as a method
hookLine: a leaf, a flower, a fruit, a little water: what the Gita says is enough

cards: A leaf. A flower. A piece of fruit.
A little water. That list came up on day eight, at the home shrine, and back then the point was how small the gifts are. Today, read the rest of the sentence.

In the ninth chapter of the Bhagavad Gita, Krishna says that whoever offers him one of these with love, he accepts it, because it was offered with love. The gift isn't what makes it count. The love is.
And the Sanskrit word for that love sits right inside the verse. A whole way of walking this path is built on it, a way full of songs, drums, bells and late nights of singing. It's today's word.

teach.b: Bhakti. Devotion. Love turned toward God and practiced on purpose, the way you'd practice an instrument.
You've spent some of this camp with the head: atman, Brahman, the self and the whole.

teach.h: THE HEART IS A PATH TOO.
teach.b: Bhakti is the heart, and the Gita treats it as a full path of its own. In the Gita's telling, nobody has to master the ideas first. The way in is love.
Devotees aim that love at God in different forms, Krishna, Rama, Shiva, the Goddess, and the move is the same. Tradition remembers a woman who showed it.
Mirabai was a princess in what is now Rajasthan, and the stories say that from childhood she thought of Krishna as her own.
Married into a royal family, she kept singing to him in the temple, in public, with ordinary devotees. Her in-laws, the stories go, were furious. They sent her poison, and it did her no harm.
Whatever you make of those details, her songs are still sung. Here's why bhakti is a method and not only a mood. Moods come and go.
The lamp gets lit anyway. The song gets sung on the tired night too.

Some who practice it say the feeling catches up with the doing, not the other way around. Go back to the leaf: what the verse looks for is the love it's offered with, and love, on this path, is something you keep doing.
That's part of why this path can be so loud. Bells, drums, a crowd singing the same name over and over. That's bhakti with the volume up.

how: Bhakti shapes Hindu worship in temples and homes: devotees sing bhajans and kirtan, offer flowers, fruit and water at home shrines and temples, and repeat the names of God, often together and out loud.

games.q: temple kitchen survived 🧅 but now i notice Nani sings to Krishna every single night, sore knees and all. dad says some nights she doesn't even feel it. so is it fake??
o: not fake. bhakti is love you keep doing, like Mirabai singing to Krishna no matter what. the feeling catches up.
yeah, if she doesn't feel it she should skip it.
it only counts if she sings in front of everyone.
games.why: Mirabai kept singing to Krishna even when her in-laws tried to stop her. Bhakti is love practiced on purpose, so Nani's song on a tired night isn't fake.

games.q: what's inside the word — tap the pairs.

s: in the leaf verse, the gift counts because of what it is
it counts because it's offered with love. the word for that love is bhakti.
bhakti is a full path of its own in the Gita
the heart is a path too. in the Gita's telling, the way in is love.
bhakti is only about feeling devoted
it's a practice. the lamp gets lit anyway, even on the tired night.

games.q: you're Mirabai. you've married into a royal family that wants you to stop singing to Krishna in public. what do you do?
o: stop singing and keep the peace.
sing only in private, where no one hears.
games.why: the stories say she kept singing, and survived even the poison her in-laws sent. her songs are still sung.

practice: The practice today: offer a leaf. Find one small thing within reach. A sip of water, a flower, a breath, even just your open hand.

Hold it for a moment. If you pray, you can offer it, with love, to God in whatever form you know. If you don't, offer it to whatever you love most in the world, and let the feeling be as big as it wants to be.
Nobody's watching. The bell holds the time.

wordCard.voice: Bhakti. Devotion. Love you practice, not only love you feel. A leaf, offered whole. Sixteenth word.

orig.note: Sanskrit: devotion, loving attention to God.

carryVoice: Your line: devotion is a verb. Today, light the lamp, sing the line, or do one loving thing, even if you don't feel like it. That's the method, all of it. Day sixteen.
